FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Food Additives Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. This standard was first published in 1977. It is being revised to take into account the latest technological advances and align it with lnternational Standards. In the revised version limits have been included for loss on drying, loss on ignition, water soluble substances, aluminium In addition, the requirements for lead, arsenic and antimony have oxide and silicon dioxide. been modified to align them with International Standards. Titanium dioxide was the first inorganic food colour approved by the Central Committee for Food Standards, Ministry of Health for permitting under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955.

The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

TITANIUM DIOXIDE,FOOD GRADESPECIFICATION ( First Revision )
1 SCOPE 1.1 This Indian Standard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for titanium dioxide, food grade. 3 REQUIREMENTS

3.1 Description Titanium dioxide shall be a white, tasteless, odourless, infusible powder. It is insoluble in water and in organic solvents. It dissolves slowly in hydrofluoric acid and hot concentrated sulphuric acid. 3.2 Identification 3.2.1 Peroxide Reaction Fuse titanium dioxide with potassium hydrogen sulphate and dissolve in water. A yellow colour shall be produced upon addition of hydrogen peroxide. 3.2.2 Spectrography The two most characteristic lines are at 4981.733 and 3653.496 A. 3.2.3 Melting Range Heat resistant to at least 500�C. to the 3.3 The material shall also conform requirements given in Table 1. for titanium

C-2 PROCEDURE C-2.1 Suspend 5 g of titanium dioxide in 100 ml of the hydrochloric acid and heat on a water-bath with occasional stirring for 30 minutes. Filter through a Gooch crucible in which the mat has been built up in 3 layers; 3

first using medium coarse asbestos; then pulped filter paper, and finally fine asbestos. The asbestos should previously have been acid washed. Wash with three, IO-ml portions of Evaporate the combined hydrochloric acid. filterate and washing to dryness in a platinum dish and ignite at a dull red heat to constant mass. The mass of the residue should not exceed 0.0175 g. Use the residue for the determination of soluble barium compounds ( E-2 ).

( Caution: This titration should be performed quickly near the endpoint by adding rapidly 0.2 ml increments of the titrant until the first color change occurs; although the colour will fade in 5 to 10 seconds, it is the true endpoint. Failure to observe the first colour change will The fading result in an incorrect titration. endpoint does not occur at the second endpoint. This first titration should require more than 3 ml of titrant, but for more accurate work a titration of 10 to 15 ml is desirable ), Add 2 g of sodium fluoride, boil the mixture for 2 to 5 minutes, and cool in a stream of running water. Titrate the EDTA ( which is by fluoride from its aluminium released complex ) with 0.01 M zinc sulfate to the same fugitive yellow brown or pink endpoint as described above. Add dropwise ammonium hydroxide solution ( 1 in 5 ) until the colour is just completely changed from red to orange yellow, then add 10 ml of ammonium acetate buffer solution ( 77 g of ammonium acetate plus 10 ml of glacial acetic acid, diluted to 1 000 ml with water ) and 10 ml of dibasic ammonium phosphate solution ( 150 g of dibasic ammonium phosphate in 700 ml of water, adjusted to pH 5.5 with a I in 2 solution of hydrochloric acid, then diluted to 1 000 ml with water ). DETERMINATION H-l FROCEDIJRE OF SILICON

Fuse 1 g of the sample, accurately weighed, Gth IO r of sodium bisulphate ( NaHSO,.&O ) contained in a 250 ml high-silica glass Erlenmeycr t7abk. Heat gently over a Maker burner, while swirling the flask, until decomposition and fusion arc complete and the melt is clear, except for the silica content, and then cool. ( Caurion: Do not overheat the contents of the flask at the beginning, and heat cautiously during fusion to avoid spzttering. ) To the cold melt add 25 ml of sulfuric acid solution ( 1 in 2 ), and heat very carefully and very slowly until the melt is dissolved. Cool, and carefully add 150 ml of water, pouring very small portions down the sides of the flask, with frequent swirling, to avoid overheating and spattering. Allow the conients of the flask to cool, and then filter through the ashless filter paper, using a 60-degree gravity funnel. Wash out all of the silica from the flask onto

the filter paper with sulphuric acid solution ( 1 in JO ). Transfer the filter paper and its cor.tents into a platinum crucible, dry in an oven at 120", and th:n heat ths partly covered crucible over a Bunsen burner. To prevent flaming of the filler paper, heat first the cover from abllve, and then the crucible from below. When the filter paper is cocsumed, transfer the rrucible to a muffle furnace and ignite at 1 000' for 30 min. Cool in a desiccator, and weigh. Add 2 drops of sulfuric acid ( I in 2) and 5 ml of concentrated hydrofluoric acid ( sp. gr. 1.15 ), and carefully evapol-ate to dryness, first on a low-heat hot plate ( to remove the HF ) and then over a Bunsen burner ( to remove the H,SO, ). Take precautions to avoid spattering, especially after removal Ignite at 1 000" for IO min, cool in of the HF. Record the a desiccator, and weigh again. the two weights as the difference between content of SiO, in the sample.

Standard Mark

The USCof the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
